item.title: Sewol Passengers Were Told To Stay As The Captain Escaped
item.description: When South Korea’s Sewol ferry sank in April 2014, passengers were told to remain inside while the captain and crew escaped. The disaster killed 304 people, mostly high school students. Captain Lee Joon-seok was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: Why The Cornell Seven Case Was Reopened
item.description: A former Cornell student’s lawsuit alleges seven fraternity members sexually assaulted her in October 2024. The defendants deny wrongdoing. After questions emerged about the original investigation, New York appointed a special prosecutor to review the evidence.

item.title: Beth Thomas Outgrew The “Child Of Rage” Label
item.description: Featured at six in the documentary Child of Rage, Beth Thomas described violent behavior following severe childhood abuse and neglect. Her story continued beyond those interviews: she later became a neonatal intensive care nurse and spoke publicly about her recovery.

item.title: Zachary Witman Said He Found His Brother. Then Confessed
item.description: In 1998, 15-year-old Zachary Witman said he discovered his younger brother Greg dead in their Pennsylvania home. Nearly 20 years later, he admitted killing him and pleaded guilty to third-degree murder. He was released on parole in 2019.

item.title: Combs’s Lawyers Used Cassie Ventura’s Texts To Challenge Her
item.description: During Sean Combs’s 2025 trial, singer Cassie Ventura faced questions about years of private messages as his lawyers challenged her account of coercion. Combs was later acquitted of sex trafficking and racketeering but convicted of two transportation-for-prostitution offenses.

item.title: Paulette Was Found In Her Bed After Nine Days
item.description: Four-year-old Paulette Gebara Farah was reported missing in Mexico in March 2010. Nine days later, investigators found her body between her mattress and the foot of her bed, despite earlier searches. Authorities ultimately concluded she died of accidental suffocation.

item.title: Lee Hae-in Challenged Her Three-Year Ban And Returned
item.description: South Korean figure skater Lee Hae-in denied allegations of sexually harassing a younger teammate, saying they were dating. A court paused her three-year ban in November 2024, finding the conduct did not constitute harassment. The skating federation lifted the ban in May 2025.
